# Editorial checklist

## Reader and purpose

- Name one primary audience and one need
- State the benefit early and give a clear next step
- Explain unfamiliar open source terms in context
- Keep each section focused on one idea

## Amadeus voice

- **Enthusiastic:** use active verbs and purposeful energy, not hype or exclamation marks
- **Genuine:** write person to person; avoid corporate, consultant and academic language
- **Expert:** be concrete and generous with knowledge; do not preach
- **Simple:** prefer short sentences, common words and sentence-case headings

Prefer `start`, `help`, `use`, `work together` and `check`. Avoid `commence`, `facilitate`, `leverage`, `empower`, `endeavor` and vague transformation claims.

## UI and links

- Buttons use a short action label, normally no more than three words
- Links describe their destination and make sense out of context
- Do not write “click here” or refer to a control by color or position
- Decorative images have empty alternatives; meaningful images get concise purpose-led alternatives

## Evidence and inclusion

- Distinguish observed facts, reported claims, interpretation and pending validation
- Include source date and scope for changing claims
- Represent code and non-code contribution without ranking people by default
- Avoid stereotypes, gendered defaults, idioms and unexplained internal language
- Never imply GitHub activity is the complete measure of open source participation

## Post quality

- Frontmatter uses all eight supported fields and a unique lowercase slug
- Body starts at `##`; the page already renders the article title
- Dates use `YYYY-MM-DD` in frontmatter
- Read time is plausible and manually reviewed
- Tags are short, reused where appropriate and not a second taxonomy
- Only the intentional lead story is featured
